model: P&C insurer FCFE at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 208.58M common on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, 2026-07-10) + 3.1M dilutive securities (Q2-2026 diluted 213.6M less basic 210.5M weighted). Held FLAT: SBC and award withholding taxes are charged in the flows, and buybacks are the distribution mechanism of the FCFE stream itself, not a separate value source.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL: ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back) TTM Q2-2026 = FY25 256 + H1-26 148 - H1-25 140 = 264; taxes withheld on net-share settlement TTM = 127 + 154 - 124 = 157 (financing activities). Summed (no combined figure published) = 421.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM Q2-2026 financing-activity repurchases = FY25 3,004 + H1-26 3,098 - H1-25 750 = 5,352, including ~$700M of Canada-sale proceeds earmarked for buybacks; FY2025 alone 3,004. Pace ~$1.3bn/quarter in 1H26; ~$3.9bn authorization remaining mid-2026. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: the flow is FCFE (pre-tax operating income is already after $425M/yr interest expense on $9.07bn debt), so net debt is held at zero and never deducted. CoE 8.5% = 10y UST ~4.2% + adjusted beta ~0.8 x 5.0% ERP + ~0.3pp for catastrophe/reserve tail not captured by a low equity beta. USD flows, USD rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial for an insurer of this scale; lease cost sits inside operating expenses in pre-tax income (single treatment, nothing in the bridge).
inputs.nci_treatment: None material; consolidated pre-tax income is attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on the owner-FCF component engine (net debt = 0), the house precedent for insurers (PRU, GL, IAG.AX, MET). The dcf-methods routing table defaults insurers to BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because Travelers does not compound book -- it distributes ~all earnings (dividends ~$1.0bn + buybacks $3-5bn/yr vs NI $5-8bn), so GAAP equity went $26.6bn (FY07) -> $33.1bn (Q2-26) while shares fell 628M -> 209M, and equity is further swung by AOCI (-$5.0bn FY24, -$2.7bn Q2-26). Engine mapping: revenue = total revenues (earned premium + NII + fees + realized gains); 'ebitda_margin' = GAAP pre-tax income margin + SBC expense add-back (0.54% of revenue) so the SBC line can be charged explicitly; D&A and capex both 0 (amortization/depreciation ~$0.7bn is already inside pre-tax income and broadly matches capitalized software/IT spend); cash tax ~20% (FY25 effective 19.3%, H1-26 19.8%, municipal-bond income shelters); 'working capital' on the CHANGE in revenue = statutory capital retained to support premium growth (-65% of incremental revenue base ~= tangible equity ex-AOCI $31.4bn / revenue $49.0bn). TTM pre-tax margin 21.1% ($10.33bn on $48.98bn) is a cycle peak (Q2-26 combined ratio 83.6%, light H1-26 cats, favourable reserve development); base fades to a 14.5% through-cycle pre-tax margin (~93% combined ratio + ~$4.3bn NII), ~16-17% ROE on ex-AOCI book, consistent with management's mid-teens core ROE objective. Cross-check (BVPS x P/B): BVPS Q2-26 $159 on 208.6M cover shares ($171 ex-AOCI); base IV ~2.4x reported book (2.6x FY25 book per sanity_check) vs a 10y FY-end average of ~1.6x and ~2.3x today -- the premium is the cycle-peak ROE, and is the main thing a bear case takes away. Canada: sale to Definity closed 2026-01-02; TTM base still holds ~6 months of Canadian premium (~$0.6bn), so year-1 growth carries a ~-1.2pp mechanical drag.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Premium/revenue growth judgment (ex-Canada BI +3-5%, B&S +14-16%, PI -8% NWP in Q2-26), not equity CAGR: equity is suppressed by full capital return and swung by AOCI.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.4% vs revenue 8.8% and EPS 21.4% -- divergence >30%. Explained: buybacks (shares -20% over 5y) and AOCI rate marks (-$5.0bn at FY24) suppress book; EPS CAGRs run from a 2022-23 cat/reserve-heavy base to a 2025-26 cycle peak and must not be extrapolated.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are operating cash flow, which for an insurer includes float growth and is not owner cash; shown for completeness only. SBC is small (0.5-0.9% of revenue) and is not a driver of growth divergence here.

base.narrative: Cycle normalises: pre-tax margin fades from the 21% TTM peak to ~14.5% by year 4 (combined ratio drifts to ~93% as property pricing softens and cat load reverts to the long-run average) while NII keeps rising on new-money yields ~90bp above book yield. Growth 3-4.5% (BI mid-single-digit, B&S double-digit fading, PI shrinking then stabilising). Capital retained at ~65c per $ of incremental revenue; everything else returned.

bull.narrative: Underwriting edge proves structural: AI/data-driven risk selection and the walk-away discipline on national property keep the combined ratio near 90% through a soft market; B&S compounds at double digits; NII tailwind persists with rates higher for longer; reserve releases continue. Pre-tax margin settles ~16.5%, growth 5-6.5%, and the market keeps paying a premium-underwriter multiple.

bear.narrative: The cycle turns hard: commercial pricing follows national property down, social inflation forces adverse casualty reserve development (GL, commercial auto, umbrella) and a heavy cat year (wildfire/convective storm) lands in years 2-3; combined ratio ~97-98% at trough before recovering to ~95%. Rate cuts stall NII. PI keeps shrinking to direct writers; growth 0.5-3%. Market de-rates TRV to a commodity-underwriter multiple.

scenario_narratives.base: Cycle normalises from a peak: TTM 21% pre-tax margin (Q2-26 combined ratio 83.6%, benign cats, favourable PYD) fades to a ~14.5% through-cycle level (~93% combined ratio plus a still-rising ~$4.3bn+ NII line) by year 4. Revenue grows 3-4.5% as Business Insurance (+3-5% ex-Canada) and Bond & Specialty (+14-16%) offset a deliberately shrinking Personal Insurance book. ~16% ROE on ex-AOCI book with the excess distributed via the $1.25/qtr dividend and buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Travelers' underwriting discipline and data/AI edge hold the combined ratio near 90% through the softening phase, reserve releases persist, and higher-for-longer rates keep NII compounding; B&S remains a double-digit grower. Pre-tax margin ~16.5% steady state, growth 5-6.5%, terminal 17x FCFE (~14x earnings), the multiple a premium underwriter has held in 2024-26.
scenario_narratives.bear: Mean reversion overshoots: commercial casualty pricing softens behind national property, social inflation forces reserve strengthening as it has at several peers, and a large cat year (2025 CA wildfire-scale, $1.7bn) recurs. Combined ratio ~97-98% at trough, NII stalls on rate cuts, PI keeps ceding share to Progressive/GEICO. Margin troughs ~10% pre-tax, recovers to ~12.5%; terminal 12x FCFE (~10x earnings), the 2011-2019 trading range.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the valuation date sits at a multi-decade peak in P&C margins with the leading indicator (national property pricing) already rolling over and casualty reserve risk industry-wide. Base 50%: normalisation to TRV's own mid-teens ROE objective is the most likely path. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (no cycle turn, continued reserve releases, rates staying high).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Travelers is valued as a distributor of free cash flow to equity: normalised after-tax underwriting plus investment income, less the capital that must be retained to support premium growth, discounted at the cost of equity with no net-debt deduction. The central judgment is margin normalisation -- the TTM 21% pre-tax margin is a cycle peak and is faded to TRV's through-cycle level; the valuation is far more sensitive to that fade than to growth.
key_risks_to_valuation: Underwriting-cycle turn: national property pricing is already softening; each 1pp of steady-state pre-tax margin is worth roughly $25-30/share.
Casualty reserve adequacy / social inflation (GL, commercial auto, umbrella): adverse development would hit book and earnings simultaneously.
Catastrophe volatility and climate trend: a 2025-wildfire-scale event ($1.7bn pre-tax) is ~4% of a year's revenue.
Rate cuts would stall the NII tailwind that underpins the base-case margin floor.
Terminal multiple: 15x FCFE base (~12.5x earnings) vs a 10-14x historical P/E range; terminal value is the majority of value.
